scenario: [LTIM.1.1.5]: the representable `Time` range includes its ends, so arithmetic that lands exactly on one raises nothing. `E` holds `near_top`, one second before the last instant (2^63 - 1 ns), and `top`, the last instant; and `near_bottom`, one second after the first (-2^63 ns), and `bottom`, the first. Rule `ends` compares `e.near_top + 1_s` with `top` and `e.near_bottom - 1_s` with `bottom`, and logs both: `true true`. Rule `handler`, which logs any ComputationError, must not fire, so a range check off by one at either end fails here. PATH PINNED: the bounds of libds's checked `Time` arithmetic in `rete/eval.c` and of the Mercury runtime's `ds.eval.ltim_1_1_5_add` and `ltim_1_1_5_sub`.
rules_ds:
schema E scope logical:
    id: Int key
    near_top: Time mutable
    top: Time mutable
    near_bottom: Time mutable
    bottom: Time mutable

rule ends:
    E e
->
    let up = (e.near_top + 1_s) == e.top
    let down = (e.near_bottom - 1_s) == e.bottom
    log info "{up} {down}"

rule handler:
    ComputationError c
->
    log critical "{c.kind} {c.rule}"
